order: Created after frozen image observations and subsequent source consultation.
reference_traits: Repeated finely divided leaf segments, narrowly linear to threadlike
Compound umbels of numerous small flowers
Yellow petals (supporting only; manuscript pigments not treated as reliable botanical colour)
Fruit shape/ribs if actually visible; not inferred from dotted forms
reference_context: Modern flora morphology, not proof that a medieval illustrator must preserve every trait. No closely matched medieval fennel drawing was visually audited: an exploratory Hartlieb1462 source lead could not be fetched and is not counted as a comparator.
lookalike_warning: Dill shares fine divisions and umbels (Kew Flora Zambesiaca). Even a positive combination would not uniquely identify fennel. Broad-leaved Apiaceae also exist, but family membership is not fennel identification.

f14v.reason: Dominant broad toothed blades and separate curled heads fail to show the filiform division / compound-umbel combination.
f14v.alternative_assessment: Fern-like or broad-leafed flowering-herb proposals remain distinct. Curled heads alone cannot choose between them. No alternative confirmed.

f18r.reason: Broad entire lower leaves and one large terminal head are more naturally compared with a head-bearing flowering herb than with fennel.
f18r.alternative_assessment: Aster/marigold proposals are structurally relevant to the terminal head, but colour, proportions and leaf details prevent confident genus/species identification.

f18v.reason: Broad palmate lobes and the solitary large elaborate terminal structure do not demonstrate fennel foliage or umbels.
f18v.alternative_assessment: Columbine/mallow proposals address broad lobed leaves better than fennel does, but the head and extraordinary root remain unexplained. Edelweiss is only a retained published proposal.

f19v.fennel: Poor visual match after detail inspection
f19v.reason: The fan-like silhouette resolves into many broad pointed serrated blades on long petioles, not repeated threadlike leaf divisions. Three isolated blue-tipped structures provide no clear compound-umbel evidence.
f19v.alternative_assessment: Cleavers could motivate a whorl/cluster comparison, but broad serrated blades and unusual flowers prevent confirmation. Nailwort is a retained proposal, not selected.

f43v.fennel: Neither drawing gives a convincing fennel match
f43v.reason: Left has broad three-part foliage and a small terminal cluster; right has broad crescent organs and elongated spike-like structures. Thin lower strands are roots, not evidence of fennel foliage. No clear compound umbels.
f43v.alternative_assessment: Knotweed/bistort and grass-like comparisons merit separate consideration for the left drawing’s root or right drawing’s structures, without assigning the shared text. The right-hand Lunaria comparison may concern schematic/alchemical tradition rather than literal modern Lunaria morphology.

f24v.reason: Round tailed leaves and separate large cups conflict with a straightforward fennel depiction.
f24v.alternative_assessment: Retain historical Lychnis? and unresolved origophyllus proposals; not an initial daro page.
